provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

value.reason: The evidence shows both GET /api/Users and GET /api/Users/:id protected only by security.isAuthorized(), which checks that the caller is logged in but not who they are. There is no check that the record belongs to the caller. /api/Users/:id takes a user-controlled id, so any logged-in user can change it and read another user's record. /api/Users returns every user. The User model holds personal profile data: email, username, role, lastLoginIp, profileImage and isActive. That fits an unscoped authenticated read and broken object-level authorization. One caveat: the handler that runs after the middleware (Juice Shop's auto-generated REST resource) isn't in the evidence, so I can't see whether it narrows the results. Nothing shown limits them to the caller, though, and the POST /api/Users snippet only cleans up registration input. Another caveat: the 'Public' exposure label is too strong, since a login is required. But anyone can register an account, so the risk to personal data stays high.
